Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller piece of the same problem. Each recursive call works on a simpler version of the input, and the process continues until it reaches a **base case**—a condition that stops further calls. Once the base case is reached, the function returns its result, and each previous call can combine its own work with the returned value to build the final answer. Think of it like a set of nested Russian dolls: each doll (call) contains a smaller doll inside, and you keep opening them until you get to the smallest one, then you put them back together in reverse order.
